answer: The Financial Studies Department (FSD) chairperson is Ghalia Nassereddine. Faculty: Associate Professors Anis El Khatib, Mohamad Tarabay, Ghalia Nassereddine; Assistant Professor Zeinab Srour; Senior Lecturer Rima Hakim; Lecturer Jamil Hammoud.

source_quote: The Financial Studies Department (FSD) offers three programs – Accounting, Finance
answer: The Financial Studies Department offers three programs, Accounting, Finance and Banking, and Business IT Management, each leading to a BBA.

source_quote: There are two main tracks in accounting: Financial Accounting and Management
answer: Accounting measures, analyzes and communicates financial information for decision-making. It has two main tracks: financial accounting (information for investors and creditors) and management accounting (information for managers). The BBA in Accounting requires 99 credits.

source_quote: The mandatory courses for the Accounting program are listed in the table below.
answer: Accounting mandatory courses: BACC 305 Intermediate Accounting I, BACC 310 Cost Accounting, BFIN 350 Credit and Financial Analysis, BACC 405 Intermediate Accounting II, BACC 450 External Auditing, BACC 460 Advanced Financial Accounting, BACC 465 Taxation, a 3-credit Major Elective, BADM 485 Co-op Work Experience, and BADM 490 Entrepreneurship.

source_quote: must study 3 credit hours of major electives. Major electives could be upper-level courses
answer: Accounting students take 3 credits of major electives, chosen with the advisor, e.g., BACC 350 Accounting Information Systems, BACC 455 Internal Auditing, BACC 470 Forensic Accounting and Fraud Detection, or BADM 480 Independent Studies.

source_quote: advisor’s approval, a student may take BADM 480 (independent studies) as a substitute
answer: Under department-specified conditions and with the advisor's approval, a business student may take BADM 480 Independent Studies as a substitute for a program mandatory course.

source_quote: Each student must complete 8 weeks of practical training in a field related to their
answer: Accounting students complete 8 weeks of practical training (BADM 485), usually in the summer of the third year, followed by a faculty member, and submit formal reports and posters and give presentations; ENGL 217 and Senior Standing are prerequisites.

source_quote: to the traditional roles of financial reporters and analysts, internal and external auditors,
answer: Accounting careers include financial reporter and analyst, internal and external auditor, cash manager, cost controller, and strategic advisor, in government agencies, businesses and industries.

source_quote: Prepare Financial Statements in accordance with International
answer: Accounting program outcomes: apply business knowledge in problem-solving; prepare financial statements under IFRS and GAAP; communicate effectively in English; identify and analyze business problems; and respond to ethical dilemmas per standard codes of conduct.

source_quote: over six semesters and two summer sessions. The second summer session should be
answer: The Accounting BBA spans six semesters and summer sessions (Community Engagement in one summer, Co-op in the last). Year 1 Fall (16 cr): BACC 205, BADM 215, BMGT 200, BITM 200, ENGL 210, MATH 207. Year 1 Spring (16 cr): BACC 255, BADM 225, BADM 235, BADM 250, BMKA 200, ENGL 217.

answer: Accounting Year 2 Fall (18 credits): BACC 305, BACC 310, BADM 230, BECN 301, BFIN 300.

source_quote: Year 2, Spring Semester (18 Credits)
answer: Accounting Year 2 Spring (18 credits): BACC 405, BECN 302, BFIN 350, BITM 300, BITM 350, a Humanities/Fine Arts Elective; Year 2 Summer: BADM 290 Community Engagement Experience (0 credits).

source_quote: BACC 450 External Auditing 3 BACC 405
answer: Accounting Year 3 Fall (15 credits): BACC 450, BACC 465, BADM 355, BADM 420, and a Social Science Elective.

source_quote: BACC 460 Advanced Financial Accounting 3 BACC 405
answer: Accounting Year 3 Spring (15 credits): ARAB 212, BACC 460, BADM 490, a 1-credit Community & Sustainability course, a Major Elective, and a Social Science Elective; Year 3 Summer (1 credit): BADM 485 Co-op Work Experience.

source_quote: This course is an in-depth study of accounting issues related to the measurement and
answer: BACC 305 Intermediate Accounting I, 3(3,0): measuring and reporting assets, liabilities and income under IFRS, the accounting framework, time value of money, financial statement preparation, and current and noncurrent assets.

source_quote: detailed accounting study of current and noncurrent assets. Prerequisite: BACC 205.
answer: The prerequisite for BACC 305 Intermediate Accounting I is BACC 205.

source_quote: knowledge of cost allocation, process costing, and joint and product costing.
answer: BACC 310 Cost Accounting, 3(3,0): continuation of BACC 255 - cost allocation, process, joint and product costing, spoilage and waste, quality-time-cost, capital budgeting and cost control.

source_quote: concentrates on capital budgeting and cost control system analysis issues.
answer: The prerequisite for BACC 310 Cost Accounting is BACC 255.

source_quote: students to dilutive securities and their effect on earnings per share. The course
answer: BACC 405 Intermediate Accounting II, 3(3,0): liabilities, stockholders' equity, dilutive securities and EPS, fair value, financial instruments, revenue recognition, accounting changes and errors, and cash flow statements under IFRS.

source_quote: of cash flows in accordance with IFRS. Prerequisite: BACC 305.
answer: The prerequisite for BACC 405 Intermediate Accounting II is BACC 305.

source_quote: concentrates on auditing the main business cycles such as the inventory, revenue,
answer: BACC 450 External Auditing, 3(3,0): international accounting and auditing standards, audit programs and procedures, and auditing inventory, revenue, expenditure and investment cycles. Prerequisite: BACC 405.

source_quote: accounting topics, including consolidated financial statements; accounting practices
answer: BACC 460 Advanced Financial Accounting, 3(3,0): consolidated statements, partnerships, multinational corporations, branches and segments, not-for-profit and governmental accounting. Prerequisite: BACC 405.

source_quote: This course covers various aspects of the Lebanese taxation system, including
answer: BACC 465 Taxation, 3(3,0): the Lebanese tax system - real-profit taxes, taxable profit, rates, non-residents, holding and offshore companies, financial institutions, employee taxes and tax on movable capital. Prerequisite: BACC 405.

source_quote: The Co-op work experience is designed to provide students with full-time work terms
answer: BADM 485 Co-op Work Experience, 1(0,1): full-time work terms in business, industry or government to apply business education, assessing attitude and work ethic and encouraging networking. Prerequisite: ENGL 217; Senior Standing.

source_quote: from identifying an opportunity and conducting a feasibility study to preparing a
answer: BADM 490 Entrepreneurship: starting a business from identifying an opportunity and feasibility study to a business plan (marketing, operations, finance), plus funding, expansion and franchising. Prerequisite: Senior Standing.

source_quote: BADM490 Entrepreneurship 3 Senior Standing
answer: The Accounting mandatory table lists BADM 490 Entrepreneurship as 3 credits.
review_note: Mandatory table (p.211) lists 3 credits, but the Accounting study plan (p.214) lists BADM 490 as 2 credits.

source_quote: Financial fitness and performance evaluation are core activities for credit officers, loan
answer: BFIN 350 Credit and Financial Analysis, 3(3,0): financial analysis of public and non-public statements - liquidity, profitability, solvency, leverage and market performance - for credit and loan officers. Prerequisite: BFIN 300.

source_quote: information systems. It introduces the student to file and database organization,
answer: BACC 350 Accounting Information Systems, 3(3,0): file and database organization, business processes and internal controls, systems development, IS management, and accounting software and spreadsheets. Prerequisites: BACC 205, BITM 300.

source_quote: The course develops an understanding and appreciation of the role of internal auditing
answer: BACC 455 Internal Auditing, 3(3,0): the role of internal auditing, standards, risk assessment, governance, ethics and audit techniques. Prerequisite: BACC 405.

source_quote: This course will cover the basic concepts of forensic accounting. Topics include
answer: BACC 470 Forensic Accounting and Fraud Detection, 3(3,0): detecting, preventing and investigating fraud, including asset misappropriation, fraudulent statements, tax fraud and electronic fraud. Prerequisites: BFIN 300 and BACC 205.

source_quote: This course focuses on advancing the student’s knowledge in their specialization
answer: BADM 480 Independent Studies, 3(3,0): independent research and application on current or emerging topics in the student's specialization, approved by the assigned faculty member. Prerequisite: advisor's approval.

source_quote: This subject provides an overview of today's accounting and financial planning
answer: BACC 210 SME's Financial Planning and Accounting, 3(3,0), a course for non-business programs: accounting and financial planning for small businesses, contractors and freelancers - budgeting, procurement, work planning, cost control and simplified financial statements, at least one-third hands-on.
